semantic_changes: The scenario driver's voter count became a parameter; the selected case runs the trimmed history with five voters instead of three.

scope.description: The trimmed case of the established scenario, run with five voters instead of three: one leader is isolated and appends sixty entries that reach no quorum, is shut down, the remaining four voters elect a leader and commit twenty further entries plus the forced snapshot with TrailingLogs=10, the isolated voter is restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected, and its restores, applied and commit indexes, cached claim, store range and the cluster frontier are sampled every 250 ms for three seconds while one entry per sample is applied on the leader.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced event is one partition of a single voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Only the voter count differs from the established three-voter case; store type, TrailingLogs, write pattern, window and sampling are identical, so a change in the signature would be attributable to the cluster size.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting stays disabled so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

basis.prefix: Same driver as the established trimmed case with the voter count parameter set to five: build the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commit sixty entries, partition the initial leader, fire sixty applies on it so they are appended without a quorum, wait for it to step down, shut it down with Shutdown().Error(), wait for one of the four remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commit twenty further entries there and force Snapshot(), restart the isolated voter with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnect it, emit ca_setup with the tag, the premise fields and the cached claim, wait until its applied index reaches the snapshot index, then sample every 250 ms for three seconds while applying one entry per sample on the leader, emit ca_probe, and disconnect the victim before bounded teardown.
basis.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded, independent of how many voters the cluster has.

comparisons.description: Five voters: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged.
Five voters progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier although new entries committed and applied elsewhere.
Five voters: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, and its store still holds that suffix.

semantic_changes: The scenario driver gained a monotonic-store parameter and an optional repair step; the two new cases use them, and only those two cases are selected for this run.
Two new comparison subjects are recorded: the monotonic case's emptied log store with a persisting claim, and the repair case's stall-then-recovery boundary.
The scenario driver's voter count became a parameter; the selected case runs the trimmed history with five voters instead of three.

before.description: Two new cases of the same three-voter history, each built on the unchanged scenario (isolated leader appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot, isolated node restarted on its real log store and reconnected). Case one repeats the trimmed configuration with a MonotonicLogStore so the install path deletes the whole log store instead of keeping a suffix above the snapshot index. Case two keeps the non-monotonic store and, once the stall is established, drives the leader's applied index past the follower's cached claim and publishes a snapshot above it, then keeps sampling to see whether the follower resumes accepting entries.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced events are a full transport partition of one voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores, and in case two additional client writes plus one forced snapshot on the leader.

Case one uses the captured MockMonotonicLogStore wrapper over InmemStore (IsMonotonic true), so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch; the leader's own snapshot trimming still uses compactLogs, as in the earlier runs.
Case two adds only: entries applied on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, then one forced Snapshot(); the stall is measured before those additions.

Reused facilities otherwise unchanged: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting remains disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by explicit calls in both cases.

prefix.before: Same scenario driver as the earlier revisions, now parameterised by log-store monotonicity and by an optional repair step. Case one: the trimmed history runs with MonotonicLogs=true; the follower's install deletes its entire log store, and the probe reports whether installs repeat, whether the follower reaches the frontier, whether the cached claim persists, and whether any suffix above the snapshot index survived in the store. Case two: the trimmed history runs as before; when the sample loop passes 1200ms it records the pre-repair applied index, restore count and cluster frontier, keeps applying entries on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, forces Snapshot() and records the new snapshot index, then continues sampling to 4s and reports whether the stall was present before the repair and whether the follower caught up afterwards.

before.description: Monotonic store: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged.
Monotonic store progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier although new entries committed and applied elsewhere.
Monotonic store: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term.

Monotonic store: the install branch deleted the whole log store, so no entry above the snapshot index survived, while the cached claim above it persisted - the distinction from the non-monotonic case.
Repair boundary: before the intervention the follower's applied index was below the cluster frontier while repeated restores were being recorded, i.e. the stall was already present.

Repair boundary: after the leader committed past the follower's cached claim and published a snapshot above it, the follower's applied index reached the cluster frontier again, so the stall ends at the claim boundary rather than being permanent.

revision_reason: Every measured case of this question used three voters, so the driver now takes the voter count as a parameter and the trimmed case is repeated with five voters, where the starved follower is one of five and the leader retains a majority of healthy followers. Scenario, stores, TrailingLogs, write pattern, window, anchors and the three assertions are otherwise identical to the decided trimmed case; the other cases remain in the file for reuse.
